name: Alpha

source.quote: Clone Robotics proudly announces that its cutting-edge humanoid android, the Clone Alpha, is now available for pre-order.
Clone is a bipedal android companion. Made for individuals and businesses alike.
Clone is manufacturing only 279 units of the limited edition Clone Alpha.

order_type.note: The /pre-order/ page hosts a free reservation form ('Reserve') for the 279-unit limited edition, with no price or checkout shown as of this build -- a preorder/reservation, not a live cart sale.

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for Alpha were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: Demo of the Clone hand only (mounted on a desk), not the full Alpha body; operator wears a sensor glove and a neural-network 'V2 Controller' translates finger/wrist motion into the artificial-muscle hand in real time. This dataset only records what is shown on camera, so this entry covers the hand demo, not a claim about Alpha's full-body teleoperation.

capabilities.note: Palm pressure pads reported to detect grip force during the same glove-teleoperated hand demo; shown affecting grip behavior on camera, not just listed as a spec.

timeline.detail: Clone Robotics announced the Clone Alpha as a limited edition of 279 home android units and opened a pre-order waitlist, with pre-orders stated to become available in 2025.

notes: No manufacturer source states Alpha's height, weight, or degrees-of-freedom with a checkable literal quote. Clone's own /research/ specs page currently reads 'We are currently researching, page will be available soon' (accessed 2026-09-20). Aggregator sites (Humanoid Index, Humanoid.guide, etc.) widely repeat figures of ~170 cm / ~60 kg / 164 DOF, but per the evidence rules these do not qualify as a claimed-status source because they do not cite a traceable manufacturer statement for those exact numbers. Specs are left empty rather than sourced to an aggregator.

No checkout price has ever been published by Clone Robotics; the pre-order page collects a waitlist signup without a stated amount, so price_history is empty rather than guessed. Clone's 2023 pitch mentioned an aspirational ~$20,000 target price, and the founder repeated a similar figure in a March 2026 interview, but neither is an orderable price.

No independent or uncut demonstration video of Alpha walking or performing tasks live could be confirmed during this build; walking is reported by trade press as a 2027 target, and the 2025 preorder window is reported to have passed without shipments. Delivery status is therefore recorded as 'claimed' (announced + preorder claim), not 'demonstrated' or 'shipped'.

Clone Robotics' operational presence is reported in Wrocław, Poland (R&D/manufacturing) while corporate/investor materials list a US entity; manufacturer.country is set to US pending a single authoritative filing, and this should be revisited if a primary source pins one jurisdiction.

review.reason: Targeted searches found no confirmed model for this record; does not mean unavailable.
